sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Condorcet Jury Convergence and Campaign Cost Budget Studio! Select between Moderate Crowd, 95 Percent SLA Redundancy, Qualified Workforce, and Anti-Condorcet Inversion, or tune worker count n, accuracy p, Gold Sentinel overhead, and unit HIT cents directly above to track collective precision and 10,000-item spend!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at those two plots above us, Nova! At p equals 0.65, raising redundancy from 9 workers to 29 pushes collective consensus from 82.83 percent past 95.24 percent while active learning trims the 10,000-item campaign from 4,950 dollars down to 1,485—yet dropping individual competence to 0.40 triggers immediate Anti-Condorcet collapse!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 1: Suppose 9 independent workers classify chest X-rays. Compare exact majority accuracy at individual competence p equals 0.65 versus an adversarial cohort at p equals 0.40, and determine what happens as pool size n keeps scaling toward infinity. Select Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Nine workers at p equals 0.65 versus inverted workers at p equals 0.40! Evaluate both binomial majority probabilities and lock in the true asymptotic limit as n scales to infinity above me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Correct! By Condorcet's binomial sum with n equals 9, individual competence p equals 0.65 achieves 82.83 percent collective accuracy and crosses 95.24 percent at 29 workers toward 100 percent. In contrast, p equals 0.40 yields only 26.66 percent—inducing Anti-Condorcet inversion that drives ensemble accuracy monotonically to zero as n increases!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Condorcet convergence holds strictly when p exceeds 0.50: at p equals 0.65 and n equals 9 accuracy hits 82.83 percent, whereas at p equals 0.40 redundancy amplifies error—dropping n equals 9 to 26.66 percent and collapsing toward zero percent as more faulty workers vote!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to the Active Entropy Query and Dawid-Skene Consensus Explorer! Dial model posterior probability and Worker C accuracy on fixed votes [1, 0, 0] above to see decision-boundary uncertainty hit 0.9997 bits and watch Dawid-Skene log-odds rescue Class 1 from a 2-to-1 adversarial majority loss!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the right-hand posterior comparison above us, Nova! Naive majority sees votes [1, 0, 0] and picks Class 0 by 67 percent to 33—yet because hidden Gold Sentinels detected Worker C flipping labels at accuracy 0.15, Dawid-Skene inverts their vote to rescue Class 1 by a +3.73 nat margin!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 2: Why do persistent managed teams outperform anonymous public crowds on autonomous-vehicle pixel segmentation, and why must every campaign pair upfront Qualification Exams with continuous 10 percent hidden Gold Sentinels? Choose Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Autonomous perception edge-snapping plus stopping mid-session fatigue after batch 50! Identify how managed cohorts and continuous 10 percent Gold Sentinels work together in the three choices above me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot on! Managed perception teams complete multi-week codebook training, sustaining competence above 0.90 and Fleiss' Kappa above 0.85 rather than anonymous boundary jitter. Meanwhile, hiding 10 percent Gold Sentinels inside live batches tracks mid-session fatigue past initial Qualification Exams to update real-time Dawid-Skene confusion estimates!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Anonymous micro-task crowds suffer high turnover and correlated edge-snapping error on complex AV polygons, while upfront Qualification Exams alone cannot detect speed-clicking or fatigue after batch 50—only continuous 10 percent hidden Gold Sentinels furnish unbiased online confusion matrices!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 3: Under the Dawid-Skene model calibrated against gold units, compare a random clicker at p equals 0.50 against a systematic label flipper at p equals 0.10, and account for Fleiss' Kappa under rare class skew. Select Option A, B, or C above me!

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Final checkpoint: random white noise at p equals 0.50 versus 90 percent inverted signal at p equals 0.10—plus the Feinstein-Cicchetti prevalence paradox at 95-to-5 skew! Lock in the exact statistical verdict above me!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding mastery! Worker X guessing at 0.50 injects pure white noise with zero log-odds and zero mutual information. Conversely, Worker Y systematically flipping labels at 0.10 exhibits 90 percent predictable inversion that Dawid-Skene flips directly back into high-value evidence—while remembering that 95-to-5 skew drives expected agreement to 0.905!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. A pure coin-flipper at 0.50 gives log odds zero and zero Shannon mutual information, so calibration cannot rescue their guesses. By contrast, a systematic flipper getting 90 percent wrong carries inverted conditional likelihoods that Dawid-Skene recovers cleanly into 90 percent accurate signal!
